routes.label: Count disjoint sets formed from the largest chosen element
Pair elements summing to the largest chosen element

officialSolution.label: 2025 AMC 12A
officialSolution.sourceTerms: The linked source retains its printed copyright notice and host terms. This project adds no copy of this PDF.

question: A set of numbers is called sum-free if whenever \(x\) and \(y\) are (not necessarily distinct) elements of the set, \(x + y\) is not an element of the set. For example, \(\{1, 4, 6\}\) and the empty set are sum-free, but \(\{2, 4, 5\}\) is not. What is the greatest possible number of elements in a sum-free subset of \(\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 20\}?\)
solution:
The largest chosen element provides a useful restriction: two chosen numbers cannot add to it.

First, \(\{11,12,\ldots,20\}\) is sum-free because any two of its elements have sum at least \(22\). Thus \(10\) elements are possible.

For an upper bound, let \(S\) be any nonempty sum-free subset, and let its greatest element be \(m\). Pair the smaller positive integers so that each pair sums to \(m\). At most one member of each pair can belong to \(S\).

If \(m=2r\) is even, the pairs are
\[
\{1,2r-1\},\ \{2,2r-2\},\ \ldots,\ \{r-1,r+1\}.
\]
These \(r-1\) pairs contain every positive integer below \(m\) except \(r\). But \(r\) cannot be chosen either, since \(r+r=m\). Including \(m\), we get
\[
|S|\leq (r-1)+1=r\leq10.
\]

If \(m=2r+1\) is odd, all integers below \(m\) form the \(r\) pairs
\[
\{1,2r\},\ \{2,2r-1\},\ \ldots,\ \{r,r+1\}.
\]
Including \(m\), this gives \(|S|\leq r+1\). Since an odd \(m\leq20\) is at most \(19\), we have \(r\leq9\), so again \(|S|\leq10\).

The upper bound is attained by the set above. Therefore the greatest possible size is \(\boxed{10}\), choice C.
